messages:
Mia Chen: FYI customer 'acme-inc' hitting 502s on hosted /v1/generate since 09:12 UTC. First noticed ~09:11:42 by their app. Correlation ids: c5f3b2a7, d9a8e1f0. Status code 502 from API gateway
Raj Patel: looking now. any pattern (tenant, model, route)?
Mia Chen: single tenant, high QPS, using model 'rw-2-8k'. Traffic spike coincides with billing window. Most failures report upstream control-plane 5xx: auth/session and routing-policy timeouts.
SRE Oncall: can you paste a sample gateway log and control-plane error?
Mia Chen: paste log snippet:
```
[09:12:03] api-gateway: req_id=c5f3b2a7 path=/v1/generate tenant=acme-inc status=502 upstream=control-plane error="503 ServiceUnavailable"
[09:12:03] ctrlplane-routing: trace=d9a8e1f0 route_eval=failed error="timeout to routing-policy service (dial tcp 10.2.5.14:443): context deadline exceeded)"
[09:12:04] auth-session: session_lookup tenant=acme-inc error="configdb read timeout after 2s"
```
Raj Patel: configdb read timeouts + routing-policy timeouts — looks like connection pool exhaustion or configdb saturated. Any recent deploys to routing-policy or config DB settings?
Alex Gomez: I rolled a small routing-policy tweak yesterday (reduced http client timeout to 200ms) to catch slow backends earlier. That could be too aggressive under sustained high QPS.
SRE Oncall: temp mitigation: bump routing-policy client timeout to 1s and enable fallback to cached routing. Mia can you apply via staging flag on the control-plane config?
Mia Chen: applying change now (flag: routing.policy.client_timeout_ms=1000, routing.policy.enable_cache_fallback=true) and toggling warm cache. Will monitor.
Support Bot: Notifying customer with standard blameless note: "We are investigating increased 502 errors; temporary mitigation underway; ETA ~15m" :hourglass:
Mia Chen: after toggle, success rate improved from 78% -> 98% within ~60s. Gateway 502s dropped.
Raj Patel: follow-up actions:
- confirm configdb connection pool metrics (max_conn, used_conn) for tenant shard
- increase configdb read timeout slightly or add request queueing at routing-policy
- add circuit breaker for routing-policy to avoid tight failure loop
- rollback the 200ms optimization and add load-based threshold for it
Alex Gomez: I'll open a PR to revert the 200ms change and add a feature flag gated by 95th p99 latency.
SRE Oncall: runbook update: document that aggressive routing-policy timeouts during billing/QPS spikes can cascade to auth/session configdb lookups causing 502s. Add checklist to enable cache-fallback and increase client timeout to 1s as first response.
Mia Chen: incident summary for support ticket: "Root cause: aggressive routing-policy client timeout + configdb connection pressure during tenant QPS spike caused control-plane to return 5xx; mitigation: increased timeout + enabled cache fallback; customer impact: transient 502s ~ 09:12-09:20 UTC; next steps: configdb pool tuning, revert/flag routing-policy change, run a replay test under load."
Support Bot: Ticket updated and customer notified of fix and next steps.
Alex Gomez: I'll schedule a small load-repro on staging with the original 200ms setting to validate PR fixes.
SRE Oncall: reopening if we see any reappearance; leaving postmortem stub in #postmortems. :white_check_mark:
Mia Chen: thanks team. Closing thread unless anything new appears.
